content.title: Mechanics of Linear Regression
content.explanation:
• Foundational supervised algorithm.
• Predicts continuous numerical values.
• Finds best fitting line.
• Learns math relationship (X to Y).
• Example: Predicting house prices.

cards.front: What calculates the total error of our model's predictions?
What is the optimization engine that updates weights to minimize error?
What do we call the 'intercept' or starting value in our equation?

content.title: Line of Best Fit
content.explanation: Minimizes the total distance between the line and all data points.

content.title: What is Loss?
content.explanation:
• Loss measures prediction error.
• High Loss = bad predictions.
• Zero Loss = perfect predictions.
• Guides model improvement.
• Like the 'Hot or Cold' game.

content.title: The Loss Function
content.explanation: The algorithm uses Loss to steer itself toward the target.

content.title: Hyperparameters vs Parameters
content.explanation:
• Hyperparameters: Set by humans.
• Parameters: Learned by machines.
• Hyperparameters control learning.
• Parameters hold the knowledge.
• Example: Learning Rate vs Weights.

content.title: Hyperparameters vs Parameters
content.explanation: You turn the dial (Hyperparameter). Internal reactions happen automatically (Parameters).

content.title: Gradient Descent
content.explanation:
• Mathematical optimization algorithm.
• Finds the absolute best answer.
• Takes small steps downhill.
• Stops at zero errors.
• Requires correct Learning Rate.

content.title: Gradient Descent Optimization
content.explanation: Steps start large when steep, and get smaller near zero loss.
diagram: Calculate gradient (slope of the error curve)

challenge.solution:
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
import numpy as np

X_train = np.array([[500], [1000], [1500], [2000]])
y_train = np.array([50, 100, 150, 200])
X_test = np.array([[1200]])

model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
prediction = model.predict(X_test)
print(f'Predicted value: {prediction[0]}')
